slides.heading: Valid Ip Addresses
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Strings
slides.narration: Let's solve Valid Ip Addresses, a medium strings problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: All ways to insert three dots into a digit string to form valid IPv4 addresses (each part 0-255, no leading zeros).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. All ways to insert three dots into a digit string to form valid IPv4 addresses (each part 0-255, no leading zeros).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Place three dots; each of the four parts must be 0 to 255 with no leading zeros.
slides.narration: Place three dots; each of the four parts must be 0 to 255 with no leading zeros.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: All dot placements: at most 3·3·3 = 27 → O(1)
slides.narration: There are at most twenty-seven ways to place three dots, so brute force is already constant time. The work is validating each part.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Try all positions for three dots
slides.narration: Step by step. First, try all positions for three dots. Second, validate each part. Third, collect valid addresses.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Try three dot positions
slides.narration: Place three dots. Each part must be one to three digits, at most 255, with no leading zero.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Leading zeros are invalid
slides.narration: Parts like zero one are invalid because of the leading zero, but a single zero is fine.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 11 valid addresses
slides.narration: In total there are 11 valid addresses for one-nine-two-one-six-eight-zero.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Three nested loops choose the dot positions, limited to three digits per part. Each split is kept if all four parts pass valid, which checks length, leading zero and the 255 limit.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is constant (bounded by 3^3 splits). Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Watch for leading zeros and parts over 255.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Explain why brute force is bounded and fine here.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Place three dots; each of the four parts must be 0 to 255 with no leading zeros.
